scope: PR-linked issues currently Open; Snapshot 2026-10-10 JST

source_rules.original_issue_body: authoritative acceptance; checklist may be partial; click issue_url for entire body

issues.title: [INKWAVE][Aim] Gamepad support has no Joy-Con / Pro Controller motion-gyro input path
acceptance_checklist: Input layer has an optional controller-motion source separate from phone DeviceOrientation.
Available Joy-Con / Pro Controller gyro data can drive aim.
Right stick and controller gyro compose without double integration.
Gyro sensitivity/inversion/recenter behavior is deterministic.
Lack of a browser/controller motion API falls back cleanly to stick-only controls.
No regression to standard gamepad buttons, touch gyro or mouse aim.

issues.title: [INKWAVE][Systems] Respawn uses a fixed spawn-pad slot instead of player-selected Squid Spawn landing
acceptance_checklist: Human respawn enters a landing-selection state.
Player can choose among legal base-region landing points and confirm launch.
Repeated respawns can select different valid positions.
Bots may use their own deterministic selection policy.
Spawn protection begins at the correct landing phase.
https://splatoon.nintendo.com/en/gameplay/
https://splatoonwiki.org/wiki/Spawner_drone

issues.title: [INKWAVE][Shooter] Splattershot flight paint has no max-2 droplet cap and uses generic spacing
acceptance_checklist: One Splattershot projectile creates at most two normal flight droplets.
Spacing comes from validated Splattershot-specific data, not inherited generic `trailEvery`.
Projectile speed changes do not silently alter the intended pattern.
Near-user/first-droplet behavior and pattern selection are independently modeled if required.
Final surface-impact paint remains independently covered by #79.

issues.title: [INKWAVE][Shooter] Splattershot uses generic cone bloom instead of the 1%-25% outer-reticle probability model
[INKWAVE][Stage] Published build has no Scorch Gorge layout
acceptance_checklist: `MAP_LAYOUTS` (or the replacement stage registry) exposes a Scorch Gorge layout in the published target.
The layout is based on the **post-Ver. 8.0** Turf War topology, not the removed prototype.
Spawn → mid → enemy-side routes match the current reference topologically.
Grates, abyss edges, major cover and elevation landmarks are present.
Paintability and Turf-score eligibility are defined for the correct surfaces.
At least one deterministic regression verifies Scorch Gorge topology/selection in the published build.
Stage-specific comparison work can run against `inkwave-public/` without referencing the deleted `game/` tree.

issues.title: [INKWAVE][Paint][要検証] アメフラシRainNum=72と公開版172回の塗り呼出の対応を校正する
[INKWAVE][壁移動] 通常の壁泳ぎでスティックを離すと高度が完全固定され、無入力の下降がない
acceptance_checklist: 現行S3実機で、通常の無入力壁泳ぎの下降を確認し、速度曲線・開始遅延を計測してから設定する。
張り付きは維持したまま下降でき、ニュートラルで無条件に外向き跳躍させない。
ノボリ溜め/発動、壁ロール、上端越え、壁の塗り切れ/敵色化を別状態として保護する。
30/60/120Hz描画の固定tick入力で下降結果が一致する。

issues.title: [INKWAVE][Slosher] 弾群が70×1＋50×7で本家4＋5弾と異なり、薙ぎ払いにも反応しない
[INKWAVE][Bug] GPU splatter/drips render as team ink but never enter the CPU ownership grid
acceptance_checklist: For fixed `seed/kind/radius`, every visually opaque normal-ink region above the agreed coverage threshold maps to the same CPU team ownership, within explicit edge AA tolerance.
The fixed `seed=0.5`, `kind='bomb'` far-spatter point above is either owned by team 0 in the CPU grid or is no longer rendered as authoritative ink.
Wall drip regions shown as team ink have matching wall ownership for swim/climb queries, or are clearly cosmetic/non-authoritative.
`coverage()` and a GPU-derived ownership mask agree within the chosen rasterization tolerance across representative shot, bomb, blast, trail, drop, line and Roller samples.
Existing `speck(... cosmetic:true)` remains explicitly cosmetic and excluded from gameplay scoring.
Team-over-team repaint ordering remains identical between CPU and GPU.

issues.title: [INKWAVE][Movement] Stealth Jump cannot apply Splatoon 3 Ver. 11.0.0's distance-based Super Jump flight penalty
acceptance_checklist: Stealth Jump is selectable only in a slot where Splatoon 3 permits it.
With Stealth Jump absent, existing AP0 / Quick Super Jump timing remains unchanged.
With Stealth Jump equipped, a qualifying long near-base ↔ farther-in jump has a longer **flight** than the same jump without Stealth Jump.
Ground preparation duration is identical with and without Stealth Jump when Quick Super Jump AP is held constant.
The additional flight duration never exceeds the verified **60-frame / ~1.0 s** maximum.
Short or non-qualifying jumps do not incorrectly receive the maximum penalty.
Quick Super Jump and Stealth Jump compose correctly rather than one replacing the other.
The exact distance curve is validated against current Ver. 11.3.0 behavior or a verified parameter interpretation before locking numeric intermediate thresholds.

issues.title: [INKWAVE][Roller] Vertical flick launches all five globs from one origin instead of S3's tiered spawn offsets
acceptance_checklist: A fixed vertical flick no longer gives all five projectiles identical launch origins.
The three Ver. 11.3.0 vertical unit groups are represented with the correct multiplicities.
Group-specific spawn-position parameters are preserved with documented reference semantics.
Existing 26f release timing, 8.5% ink cost, vertical damage aggregation, damage bands, gravity/drag, and landing paint behavior are unchanged unless separately audited.
Add a deterministic regression test that records `p.start` before the first simulation integration and checks the expected group structure.

issues.title: [INKWAVE][Physics] Neutral Splat Bomb launch collapses separate S3 Y/Z spawn speeds into one rotated scalar
acceptance_checklist: Stationary, 0 AP, neutral aim reproduces the configured S3 base vertical/forward component pair rather than `20.0711 / 64.5829`.
Changing player `vel.y` tests player-motion inheritance independently from #237.
Downward aim tests remain separate from #238.
0 / 10 / 57 AP verify Sub Power behavior without corrupting the base vertical component.
Actual projectile and trajectory preview use identical launch components.
Gravity remains the active S3 profile value `57.6`; do not regress the existing adapter patch.
Wall/floor collision, fuse, and damage behavior remain unchanged by this fix.

issues.title: [INKWAVE][Roller] Horizontal flick collapses S3 spatial spawn width into one common projectile origin
acceptance_checklist: A deterministic horizontal flick no longer gives all 12 projectiles identical launch origins.
The 12-projectile wide-swing group preserves the reference nonzero spawn-width behavior.
Spawn-position randomness is controlled by a deterministic seeded test.
Existing 21f release timing, 8.5% ink cost, horizontal angular spread, gravity/drag, and damage aggregation remain unchanged unless separately audited.
Add a pre-integration regression test that inspects all 12 `p.start` vectors.

issues.title: [INKWAVE][Aim] Controller sensitivity uses 0.2×–3.0× instead of Splatoon 3's −5…+5 right-stick scale
acceptance_checklist: S3 fidelity mode exposes right-stick sensitivity on **−5…+5**, not 0.2×…3.0×.
Setting **0** uses a measured/calibrated S3-equivalent response rather than assuming INKWAVE 1.0× is equivalent.
At measured anchor settings (e.g. −5 / 0 / +5), a fixed full-stick trace matches the accepted S3 turn-rate tolerance.
Intermediate settings are produced by the documented/validated mapping.
Gyro sensitivity remains an independent setting.
With gyro enabled, right-stick vertical ownership follows the separate gyro-axis issue and is not changed accidentally.
Existing Standard Gamepad dead-zone handling and button bindings remain unchanged.

issues.title: [INKWAVE][Shooter] Splattershot flight droplets vanish above a 4u drop instead of using S3 fall-height paint scaling
acceptance_checklist: A Splattershot flight droplet emitted 5u above an unobstructed paintable floor lands and paints; it is not discarded.
Tests below 3u, between 3u and 10u, at 10u, and above 10u verify the expected height-dependent footprint behavior.
No hard paint/no-paint discontinuity occurs at 4u solely because of a raycast limit.
Droplet footprint is no longer randomized independently of fall height for the S3 shooter path.
Existing #129 tests for max count/spacing and #79 tests for final impact paint remain separate and continue to pass.

issues.title: [INKWAVE][Movement] Drop Roller is absent from Super Jump landing
acceptance_checklist: Drop Roller is selectable only as a legal shoes primary.
Without Drop Roller equipped, Super Jump landing behavior is unchanged.
With Drop Roller equipped and valid pre-landing direction input, a directional landing roll occurs.
Different stick directions produce corresponding roll directions.
No valid direction input => ordinary landing.
A successful roll grants temporary effective **30 AP** Run Speed Up / Swim Speed Up / Ink Resistance Up for about **3 s**, then cleanly expires.
Temporary AP does not permanently alter the gear loadout.
Normal Squid Roll state / chain logic is not reused in a way that changes its behavior.
Tests cover at least teammate Super Jump landing; Inkjet / Zipcaster returns should use the same validated mechanic once those return paths exist.

issues.title: [INKWAVE][Roller] Low-ink flicks are rejected instead of using Splatoon 3 depletion attacks
acceptance_checklist: A low-but-nonempty tank state that qualifies for the reference depletion attack no longer produces only `_empty()`.
Horizontal depletion mode emits the verified reduced S3 projectile set, including **3** projectiles instead of the normal **12**.
Horizontal depleted projectile speed applies the verified **0.5** rate.
Horizontal depleted damage applies the verified **0.25** rate before the existing distance/time falloff pipeline.
Depleted collision/paint scaling uses the corresponding S3 depletion fields.
Vertical depletion mode is configured from its own grouped S3 depletion parameters rather than reusing horizontal constants.
Normal swings at sufficient ink retain their current normal cost/timing path.
Add deterministic tests for:
sufficient ink normal horizontal;
insufficient-but-depletion-eligible horizontal;
sufficient ink normal vertical;
insufficient-but-depletion-eligible vertical;
true empty/non-fire boundary.

issues.title: [INKWAVE][ギア/索敵] リベンジがなく、自分を倒した相手の死亡まで続く本人限定追跡を使えない
acceptance_checklist: フクの基本枠限定で選択・保存でき、アタマ/クツ/追加枠では拒否。
「誰を誰が追跡しているか」を所有者別に保持。最後の1人のHUD文字列を追跡状態の代用にしない。
復活後の確実な発動ケースで本人限定の壁越しsilhouetteを表示し、味方へ漏らさない。潜伏/近距離抑制は校正条件付きで扱う。
対象生存中は16秒で失効させず、対象死亡で解除し、その対象の次の生存期間へ持ち越さない。
本人の攻撃による有効対象へのトドメが本人に帰属する基本ケースで+45F、SPの追加15パーセントポイントを適用。ここで本人による撃破とはメインの「直撃」限定という意味ではない。味方や環境による撃破ではリベンジの追加分を適用しない。相打ち/死後弾の発動境界は上記留保を維持する。
既存の#91基礎復活時間、#116、#348、PR #317の情報表示と合成し、加算重複やチーム全体へのrevealを防ぐ。
相打ち/死後弾の正確な開始時刻、特殊ギア/ドリンク併用、onlineのactor-ID再利用は、根拠と専用テストなしに完了扱いしない。
次試合への状態持ち越し、切断相手へのstale追跡を防ぐ。

issues.title: [INKWAVE][Perf] Music volume 0 keeps the 25 ms procedural scheduler and note synthesis running
[INKWAVE][Movement] Main-fire movement keeps 1× acceleration/deceleration instead of Splatoon 3's 2× attack rate
acceptance_checklist: With identical current velocity and full movement input, sustained main-fire acceleration is **2.0×** normal-state acceleration before target-speed clamping.
With identical current velocity and neutral/reverse input, sustained main-fire deceleration is **2.0×** normal-state deceleration where the reference attack rule applies.
Final firing movement speed remains the validated weapon-specific target; doubling acceleration must not double top speed.
Normal non-attacking acceleration/deceleration remains unchanged by this issue.
Enemy-ink handling, airborne control, Squid Roll, Dualies dodge roll, hard-landing recovery and wall movement do not regress.
Add fixed-60-Hz regression cases for normal vs firing acceleration and normal vs firing braking at multiple equal starting speeds.
Validate the result by the dimensionless 2× state ratio; do not rely on self-referential Nintendo-to-INKWAVE world-scale conversion.

issues.title: [INKWAVE][Movement] Comeback is absent, so its 20s 10-AP run/swim boost never applies
acceptance_checklist: Comeback is selectable only in the headgear main slot; it is not a sub ability and cannot be put on clothing/shoes through normal loadout validation.
Opponent-caused splat + respawn activates Comeback for **20.0 s**.
During that window, Run Speed Up behavior is exactly equivalent to adding **10 AP** to the same loadout's existing Run Speed Up calculation.
During that window, Swim Speed Up behavior is exactly equivalent to adding **10 AP** to the same loadout's existing Swim Speed Up calculation.
At **20.0 s**, both temporary movement contributions expire cleanly without changing permanent AP.
Environmental/self death does not activate Comeback.

Repeated ordinary movement, firing movement, swim movement, enemy-ink handling, Squid Roll/Surge, and Super Jump do not gain a separate flat WU boost; they should only observe the relevant existing AP-derived modifiers.
Existing Flow Aura / Drop Roller / permanent gear stacking remains independent and follows the same AP cap/composition rules.
No acceptance value depends on assuming INKWAVE world units equal Nintendo DU/meters.

issues.title: [INKWAVE][Perf] Offline pause keeps full scene/composer and shadow rendering at rAF cadence
acceptance_checklist: Offline `match.paused === true` freezes match time, actors, bots and projectiles as today.
After the initial pause presentation frame, repeated RAF callbacks do not cause full scene/composer renders at gameplay cadence unless the frozen world is explicitly invalidated.
Shadow maps do not refresh continuously during offline pause.
`G.paint.flush()` and world-only environment/decor/props/rig updates do not run continuously solely because RAF is alive.
Pause menu navigation/animation remains responsive.
Resume restores normal rendering immediately with no camera/input jump and no large-dt simulation step.
Online pause behavior remains intentionally live and is not accidentally frozen.
LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH/ULTRA and touch/desktop paths obey the same local-pause lifecycle contract.
Repeated pause/resume cycles do not create RAF/timer/listener leaks.

issues.title: [INKWAVE][Roller] Rolling contact applies damage but omits S3 roller-body knockback responses
acceptance_checklist: A survivable rolling contact changes post-contact velocity according to the Roller-specific collision response rather than damage-only behavior.
Opponent contact uses the S3 opponent-response branch.
Roller-player response distinguishes damage-on vs damage-off behavior.
Existing roll damage remains independently configurable and is not double-applied.
Networked hits reproduce the same authoritative collision response as local hits.
Add deterministic tests covering victim and Roller velocity before/after contact.

issues.title: [INKWAVE][Systems] Super Jump rejects teammates who are already Super Jumping instead of inheriting their destination
acceptance_checklist: A living teammate already charging a Super Jump can be selected where Splatoon 3 permits it.
A living teammate already in Super Jump flight can be selected where Splatoon 3 permits it.
The new jump lands at the first jumper's committed destination, not at their transient `pos`.
A chain A -> B -> C resolves deterministically to the committed destination represented by B's jump.
Dead/otherwise invalid teammates remain unselectable.
The fix for #362's normal-target snapshot/cancel behavior does not regress this special-case destination inheritance.
Keyboard, controller, and touch teammate selection use the same rule.
Add deterministic regression coverage for selection during both target charge and target flight.

issues.title: [INKWAVE][Perf] Main menu preloads and pins large LobbySet canvas atlases before Online is ever opened
acceptance_checklist: Staying in main/settings/loadout offline for more than 2.5 seconds without opening Online does not retain the complete LobbySet indefinitely.
Starting an offline match after menu idle releases or never allocates unused LobbySet resources.
No never-shown LobbySet can remain page-lifetime pinned solely because `L.preload === true`.
Opening Online still succeeds and does not show missing/deferred textures.
Repeated Online enter/leave cycles keep `renderer.info.memory.textures/geometries` bounded.
LOW/mobile has a documented bounded memory budget for any retained lobby atlases.
Canvas/JS memory after an unused preload is released returns near the pre-preload baseline after GC/browser reclamation.
Existing lobby cross-fade, character staging, reflection, team-color rebake and first-open behavior remain correct.

issues.title: [INKWAVE][Mobile] Visibility-only backgrounding can leave hardware-keyboard input stuck on resume
[INKWAVE][Roller] Dash turning never uses S3 SpeedDashTurnBreak and stays at 0.132/frame
acceptance_checklist: Straight rolling before 90f targets 6.48 world-units/s.
Straight rolling from 90f onward targets 7.92 world-units/s.
A qualifying hard turn while dashing invokes the S3 turn-break path and no longer carves the turn at a 7.92 target.
The turn-break target corresponds to `SpeedDashTurnBreak = 0.108/frame` (6.48 world-units/s with the current scale).
Returning to a valid dash direction/state recovers according to S3 behavior rather than permanently disabling dash.
Normal humanoid turning, Squid Roll, flick movement, roll damage, and roll paint remain unchanged.
Add deterministic coverage for straight normal roll, straight dash, dash hard-turn, and dash recovery.

issues.title: [INKWAVE][Systems] Ink Storm special gauge is emptied instantly instead of draining after use
acceptance_checklist: Activating the S3 Ink Storm mapping does **not** set the special gauge to zero on the activation tick.
After use, gauge state decreases monotonically through an explicit used-special depletion interval and reaches zero only at the end of that interval.
Normal special charging cannot begin again while the used Ink Storm gauge is still draining.
The HUD and gameplay read the same depletion state; there is no cosmetic-only drain layered over an already-zero authoritative gauge.
If the player is splatted during the Ink Storm post-use drain interval, the ordinary unused-gauge death reduction is not incorrectly applied.
A deterministic fixed-step test covers activation tick, an intermediate drain point, final zero, recharge unlock, and splat during drain.
Specials that are intended to deplete immediately retain their own semantics.
Existing Ink Storm cloud duration, radius, damage/movement behavior and projectile replication do not regress.
#76, #177 and #192 remain independently scoped.

issues.title: [INKWAVE][Match] Battle start skips Splatoon 3 Squid Spawn and fixes players to spawn-pad positions
acceptance_checklist: Normal S3 Turf War no longer places players directly on `spawnPads[team]` before GO.
All four teammates have individual initial Spawner origins/slots.
The local player can choose a valid opening landing point in the team's spawn region.
Two different selected points produce measurably different initial landing coordinates and opening travel routes.
The start signal launches the player from the Spawner in squid/octopus form instead of simply enabling ground control.
Online peers see the same selected target and launch trajectory for each player.
Invalid/enemy-side landing points are clamped/rejected by the stage's allowed initial deployment region.
Bots choose valid, deterministic/reasonable initial landing points rather than all spawning on the current fixed ring.
Post-splat respawn behavior remains separately covered by #273.
Initial spawn protection remains separately covered by #308.
Boss mode is not accidentally forced into the Turf War Squid Spawn path.

issues.title: [INKWAVE][Bug] Online paint events are unauthenticated and can alter authoritative turf and the winner
acceptance_checklist: Valid owner paint still applies exactly once.
Ownership-mismatched paint events do not mutate authoritative turf state.
Duplicate/stale events do not double-apply paint or score.
Host/adoption transitions invalidate old ownership safely.
Final coverage/winner calculation uses only admitted authoritative paint.
Existing network projectile/bomb/storm and paint-visual regressions stay green.

issues.title: [INKWAVE][Motion] Splat Dualies dodge-roll targets 2.8 units instead of S3's 5.0 DU trajectory
acceptance_checklist: On flat unobstructed ground, one Splat Dualies dodge covers **5.0 DU total** from roll start through its brief slide, within a small deterministic integration tolerance.
The displacement is direction-independent for forward/back/left/right inputs.
Two chained rolls cover approximately twice the single-roll displacement before collision corrections.
The movement-animation phase itself remains **12f**.
The separate **4f startup** remains independently testable and is not hidden by increasing `rollTime`.
Post-roll shot admission remains 4f after the roll animation and the 28f tail remains separate.
30/60/120 Hz rendering yields the same fixed-simulation endpoint.
Collision should truncate/resolve the path rather than increasing total displacement.

issues.title: [INKWAVE][Movement] Squid Roll disables mid-air stick acceleration-steering for its 15F action window
acceptance_checklist: During an active floor Squid Roll, changing only the stick after launch changes horizontal velocity **before the 15F action window ends**.
Full input in the current travel direction can increase horizontal speed during the roll when below the applicable S3 cap.
Neutral input during the roll produces natural horizontal deceleration instead of a 15F frozen velocity.
A 90° post-launch stick change creates measurable lateral velocity before roll-state expiry.
Opposite post-launch input begins redirecting/decelerating before roll-state expiry.
Vertical Squid Roll airtime/action duration remains unchanged by those horizontal stick cases.
Collision clipping remains authoritative and does not get overwritten by stored `vx/vz`.
Chain-retention, roll admission angle/min-speed, wall-roll admission, armor, and full-cancel behavior remain independently covered.
Fixed-step traces are identical at 30/60/120 Hz render rates.
Owner/network playback does not apply steering twice.

issues.title: [INKWAVE][Charger] Partial-charge movement is pinned to full-charge speed instead of Splatoon 3's 0.96→0.21 curve
acceptance_checklist: No-gear Splat Charger charging movement is not constant across all partial charges.
Minimum/no-charge endpoint maps to S3 **0.96** (profile-equivalent **5.76 u/s**).
Maximum-partial endpoint maps to S3 **0.21** (profile-equivalent **1.26 u/s**).
True full charge maps to S3 **0.20** (profile-equivalent **1.20 u/s**).
Minimum legal **8F** partial charging uses the minimum-side movement behavior rather than the full-charge endpoint.
The partial movement curve is deterministic at fixed simulation ticks and rendering at 30/60/120 Hz does not change the results.
Run Speed Up behavior remains independently covered by #243.
Full-charge jump behavior remains independently covered by #251.
Damage/range/ink/laser/charge-keep/paint behavior is unchanged.

issues.title: [INKWAVE][Damage] Blaster explosions omit Splatoon 3 knockback and never push hit players
acceptance_checklist: The active Splatoon 3 Blaster profile/runtime preserves `KnockBackParam.Accel = 700`, `Bias = 0.8`, and `Distance = 3.5` (or an explicitly validated equivalent representation).
A deterministic non-direct blast hit inside the validated knockback region produces a nonzero authoritative victim displacement/velocity response.
A target outside the validated knockback region does not receive the response.
Friendly/dead/LOS-rejected targets remain unaffected.
Knockback direction is deterministic from explosion/target geometry.
70→50 damage calculation remains independently testable.
Direct-hit behavior is validated separately against the S3 priority semantics rather than guessed from the indirect-blast test.
Network ownership tests verify that one blast causes one authoritative knockback, not duplicate owner/remote impulses.
Existing damage, terrain collision, blast FX/audio, and hit-confirm behavior do not regress.

issues.title: [INKWAVE][Systems] Tidal Slam empties the special gauge instantly instead of the Triple Splashdown through-landing drain
acceptance_checklist: Activating Tidal Slam at a full gauge does **not** set `actor.special` to zero on the activation tick.
During `rise/hang/fall`, `actor.special` decreases monotonically and deterministically.
At the landing instant, the gauge reaches the reference one-segment state rather than zero.
The final segment becomes zero when the player-body landing action completes.
A splat during a vulnerable Tidal Slam phase starts death preservation from the then-current nonzero gauge.
Special Saver modifies that remaining interrupted-use gauge through the existing actor-local S3 modifier path.
A normally completed Tidal Slam ends at zero gauge.
A nonzero in-action gauge cannot be used to start another special while `specialActive` is live.
HUD special fill follows the same `actor.special` progression; no visual-only duplicate timer.
Ink Storm's separately tracked gauge lifecycle (#469) is unchanged.
Tidal Slam protection timing (#573), Super Jump activation (#577), and spawn-barrier behavior (#582) remain separate.
Fixed-step results are identical under 30/60/120 Hz rendering.

issues.title: [INKWAVE][Charger] Earliest legal 8f shot consumes 3.00% ink instead of Splatoon 3's 2.25%
acceptance_checklist: Releases before 8F remain governed by the separate minimum-release rule.
At exactly the first legal 8F release boundary, ink consumed is **2.25% ± test epsilon** with no Ink Saver gear.
Full 60F charge still consumes **18.0%**.
The consumption curve between 8F and 60F is monotonic and follows the verified S3 parameterization rather than the generic INKWAVE S-curve by accident.
Low-ink / empty-tank behavior remains independently testable and does not permit negative ink.
Ink Saver (Main) scales the corrected base values through the existing gear path without changing the 8F timing gate.
Fixed simulation produces the same result regardless of 30/60/120 Hz render cadence.

issues.title: [INKWAVE][Match] Damaged players lack Splatoon 3 Ver. 11.0+ remaining-health bars
acceptance_checklist: A damaged visible opponent shows an approximate remaining-health bar above their head.
The opponent bar expires at approximately 3 seconds after the latest qualifying damage if no new damage arrives.
New damage refreshes the opponent display lifetime.
A normally hidden opponent behind terrain does not expose the bar.
A normally submerged opponent does not expose the bar.
A damaged teammate exposes an approximate remaining-health bar.
Full-health players do not retain stale damaged-state bars.
Splat/respawn clears stale health-bar state.
When a supported S3 reveal effect marks an opponent, that reveal can keep the health bar visible under the same conditions as the reference.
Offline and online behavior agree without leaking HP beyond the reference visibility rules.

issues.title: [INKWAVE][Motion] Splat Dualies cannot dodge-roll in midair while Splatoon 3 allows airborne slides
acceptance_checklist: With Splat Dualies, `grounded === false`, a valid firing state, valid movement direction, enough ink, and a roll remaining, fresh B/Jump starts a dodge.
The airborne dodge consumes exactly one roll and the normal dodge ink cost.
The airborne dodge produces a rapid downward/diagonal trajectory matching pinned current-S3 evidence.
The procedural Character enters the dodge/tumble presentation from the same authoritative runner state.
Landing during the air roll transitions exactly once into the intended post-roll/turret recovery.
Landing does not replay the roll or double-consume ink / roll count.
Without firing, without a valid direction, or with no rolls remaining, the same airborne B input does not start a Dualies dodge.
Grounded dodge behavior remains independently covered; #477's missing 4F startup is not hidden by this fix.
#532 trajectory/distance calibration remains independently testable.
Post-roll shooting, squid-form, ink-recovery, ordinary-Jump admission, and roll-count recovery remain independently testable.
30/60/120 Hz rendering produces identical fixed-simulation admission and landing-transition ticks.
Exact airborne vertical constants are backed by current Splatoon 3 parameter/capture evidence before being encoded.

issues.title: [INKWAVE][Physics] Splat Roller roll contact can damage opponents through solid walls
acceptance_checklist: A roller and opponent separated by a thin solid wall cannot deal/receive roll-contact damage.
Rolling parallel to a solid wall cannot damage an opponent on the opposite side even when the opponent center lies inside the current `fwd/lat/dy` rectangle.
A solid corner between drum and opponent blocks the contact.
Removing the wall with identical transforms restores the 125-damage contact hit.
A target on the same unobstructed side at the same local distance is still hit.
Non-solid/pass-through grate semantics are preserved rather than globally treating every stage surface as opaque.
Existing roller collision-width calibration remains unchanged.
The result is deterministic at the authoritative fixed simulation rate and does not depend on render Hz.

issues.title: [INKWAVE][Damage] Ink Storm throw animation freezes HP recovery during the special-active window
acceptance_checklist: A recovery-eligible, non-submerged player gains **0.21 HP/F = 12.6 HP/s** during Ink Storm throw at 60 Hz.
The normal **60F** post-hit wait still applies.
Allied Ink Storm recovery remains the separate **1.75 HP/F = 100 HP/s** path and does not stack with itself or submersion.
HP caps at 100.
Ink Storm movement/input behavior is unchanged.
No unrelated ink refill or enemy-ground contact damage is introduced.
Activation and exit boundary ticks do not double-apply recovery.
30/60/120 Hz fixed-step schedules are time-equivalent.
Existing #50/#195 normal-path recovery discrepancies remain separately testable.

issues.title: [INKWAVE][Perf] Frustum-culled actors keep Character pose, foot-IK raycasts and hair simulation running every tick
acceptance_checklist: In a 10 s camera-away test, frustum-culled non-local actors no longer execute `Character._ground()` at simulation cadence.
Long-offscreen actors show a material reduction in `Character.update/_buildPose/_applyPose/_updateHair` CPU time.
Authoritative Actor position, collision, weapons, damage, networking and AI remain unchanged.
